answers.question: When the redundancy came through, what hit you hardest in that first moment of honesty?
answers.answer: Honestly? A quiet sense of relief — I'd been ready to do something different for a while

answers.question: At SwiftCart you were running warehouse ops, managing 40+ merchant relationships, coaching your team, and building SOPs — all at once. Which of those did you find yourself doing at 6pm without noticing the time had passed, and which did you put off until you had no choice?
answers.answer: The SOP work, every time. Someone brings me a messy half-broken process and I lose the evening turning it into a checklist a new hire could follow — that never felt like work. What I put off: anything where I was being measured on someone else's KPI dashboard. The weekly merchant performance reports went out at the last possible hour, every week.

answers.question: You've promoted 4 associates to supervisor and built an SOP library that cut ramp-up time in half. When you picture doing that kind of work going forward, what's the version that actually excites you?
answers.answer: Going into a struggling operation, fixing the system, then leaving — the turnaround is the job

answers.question: A well-funded logistics scale-up offers you an Operations Manager role — good salary, real scope, but their processes are already set and your job is to execute, not redesign. Meanwhile a smaller e-commerce merchant offers you a fractional Head of Ops role at 60% of that salary, but you'd build the system from scratch. What do you do?
answers.answer: Take the fractional role — building from scratch is where I actually do my best work

answers.question: You consolidated 11 vendors down to 4 and saved S$180,000 — that required both analytical rigour and commercial negotiation. Which part of that project did you find most satisfying?
answers.answer: The implementation — getting the team to actually adopt the new supplier relationships

answers.question: Which of these would make you quietly miserable within 12 months, even if the pay was right?
answers.answer: Running operations where the processes are already mature and my job is to maintain, not improve

answers.question: Outside of your job description — what do colleagues, warehouse leads, or merchant contacts actually come to you for? The thing they message you about on a Saturday, or pull you aside for before a meeting officially starts.
answers.answer: Untangling messy processes — people bring me chaos and I turn it into a checklist. And outside work... every Chinese New Year I bake about 40 tins of pineapple tarts for family and friends. I run it like a production line — my nieces on pastry balls, me on jam, quality check before anything goes in a tin. I lose whole afternoons and it never feels like work.
